paper_metadata.title: White matter during concussion recovery: Comparing diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI)

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a well-defined source population of university athletes with clear diagnostic criteria and a matched control group. Baseline characteristics are thoroughly reported.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 66 athletes were recruited from seven university teams (volleyball, hockey, soccer, football, rugby, basketball, and lacrosse) at a single institution, via the university sport medicine clinic.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the setting (university sports teams), the specific sports involved, and the recruitment source (sports medicine clinic).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: For concussed athletes, diagnosis was determined by staff physician following events where athletes sustained direct or indirect contact to the head with the presence of signs and/or symptoms.
items.reasoning: The recruitment process via a specialized clinic and the diagnostic protocol by physicians are clearly stated.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: All athletes were recruited and imaged at the start of their respective seasons
items.reasoning: While the timing relative to the sports season is mentioned, the specific calendar years of recruitment are not explicitly stated in the text.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: at a single institution, via the university sport medicine clinic... St. Michael's Hospital in Toronto
items.reasoning: The geographic location (Toronto) and specific clinical setting are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: diagnosis was determined by staff physician following events where athletes sustained direct or indirect contact to the head with the presence of signs and/or symptoms... scanned within 7 days after concussion and at RTP
items.reasoning: Diagnostic criteria and the 'zero time' (within 7 days of injury) are clearly defined.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a notable dropout rate (approx. 18% by RTP), and while the reasons are mentioned, there is no detailed comparison of characteristics between those who completed the study and those lost to follow-up.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: From the initial design, 2 athletes could not be scanned at symptomatic injury (N = 31 remaining) and 5 athletes had missing RTP data (N = 27 remaining).
items.reasoning: Out of 33 recruited concussed athletes, only 27 (81.8%) provided complete longitudinal data. This is borderline for low risk.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (DTI and NODDI metrics) are measured using standardized, objective MRI protocols and state-of-the-art processing pipelines.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: voxel-wise DTI metrics including fractional anisotropy (FA), axial diffusivity (AD), and radial diffusivity (RD)... neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI)... orientation dispersion index (ODI), VISO, VIC
items.reasoning: All imaging parameters are mathematically defined and the measurement method (MRI) is detailed.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Participants were imaged at St. Michael's Hospital using an MRI system operating at 3 Tesla (Magnetom Skyra, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany)... FMRIB Software Library (FSL) was used to perform simultaneous correction of eddy current distortions and rigid-body head motion
items.reasoning: The use of 3T MRI and standard FSL/DTI-TK pipelines ensures high measurement reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The diffusivity components were analyzed instead of mean diffusivity (MD)... voxel-wise mean difference
items.reasoning: The study treats the imaging metrics as continuous variables in a voxel-wise analysis, avoiding arbitrary cut-points.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Participants were imaged at St. Michael's Hospital using an MRI system operating at 3 Tesla (Magnetom Skyra, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany) with the standard multi-channel head receiver coil.
items.reasoning: All participants were scanned at the same center using the same hardware and protocol.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: N = 31 remaining [at SYM] and 5 athletes had missing RTP data (N = 27 remaining).
items.reasoning: While some subjects were lost, the imaging data for the analyzed sample was complete.

risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcomes (symptom resolution and RTP) are based on standardized clinical consensus guidelines (SCAT3 and graded protocols).

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Days to RTP was determined as the number of days from the concussion event to complete symptom resolution, following a graded exertional protocol (McCrory et al., 2017).
items.reasoning: The outcome (RTP) is clearly defined based on international consensus statements.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: pre-season assessments with the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 3 (SCAT3) (Guskiewicz et al., 2013) to evaluate symptoms, cognition and balance
items.reasoning: The SCAT3 is a validated and standard tool in sports medicine for this purpose.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement

items.evidence_snippet: All athletes... had pre-season assessments with the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 3 (SCAT3)

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).

items.reasoning: The NPLS model accounts for the inter-relationships between multiple variables simultaneously.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is sophisticated, using both univariate and multivariate methods with appropriate non-parametric bootstrapping and multiple comparison corrections.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Significance was evaluated nonparametrically by bootstrapping the mean in a repeated-measures design (1,000 iterations)... cluster-size thresholding at p = 0.05
items.reasoning: The analytical steps, including bootstrapping and spatial thresholding, are described in detail.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: The NPLS 'voxel saliences' and 'diffusion parameter saliences' reflect the combination of brain regions and DTI/NODDI parameters that have maximal covariation between athlete groups
items.reasoning: The use of NPLS is justified by the need to handle high-dimensional, correlated imaging data.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: As a latent variable model, it is also robust to high-dimensional, highly-correlated data
items.reasoning: NPLS is highly appropriate for multi-shell diffusion MRI data where parameters are inherently linked.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Univariate analyses of the DTI parameters derived from the 64-direction data found no significant effects of concussion and are therefore not further discussed in this article.
items.reasoning: The authors transparently report which analyses were non-significant and why they focused on specific shells.
